dataset.title: Compatibility rules
dataset.description: Engineering compatibility rules (master prompt §44). Editable, versioned, source-tagged; DRAFT until TEAL reviews them. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation.

records.name: Laser wavelength within galvo mirror coating range

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF laser wavelength = X THEN the scanner mirror coating range must contain X (reflectivity and damage threshold are specified only inside the coating band).

records.name: Laser wavelength within f-theta design range

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF laser wavelength = X THEN the f-theta design / coating range must contain X (focus position, field distortion and transmission are specified only inside it).

records.name: Laser wavelength within beam-expander range

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF laser wavelength = X THEN the beam-expander coating range must contain X.

records.name: Laser wavelength within optic coating range

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF laser wavelength = X THEN the optic coating range must contain X.

records.name: Laser power within galvo rating

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF laser power > scanner rated power THEN incompatible (mirror heating and coating damage).

records.name: Laser power within f-theta rating

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF laser power > lens rated power THEN incompatible (thermal lensing, coating damage).

records.name: Laser power within head rating

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF laser power > head / delivery rated power THEN incompatible.

records.name: Expanded beam fits the galvo aperture (10 % margin)

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: Output beam × 1.1 ≤ scanner aperture, otherwise the beam clips on the mirrors. Check with the 1/e² diameter at your laser’s actual beam size.

records.name: Raw beam fits the galvo aperture (10 % margin)

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: Without an expander, raw beam × 1.1 ≤ scanner aperture.

records.name: Galvo aperture matches f-theta entrance beam

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: A scanner aperture larger than the lens entrance beam specification can pass a beam the lens is not designed for. Confirm the actual beam diameter at the lens.

records.name: Chiller capacity covers the laser heat load

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF heat load > chiller cooling capacity THEN incompatible. Add margin for ambient and set-point.

records.name: Lens image circle covers the camera sensor

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF camera sensor size > lens supported sensor size THEN incompatible (vignetting at the corners).

records.name: Camera and lens mount match

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: Camera and lens mounts must match. Some combinations (C lens on CS camera) work with an adapter ring — record that as a conditional relationship with evidence.

records.name: Camera and vision controller share an interface

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: The camera interface (GigE Vision, USB3 Vision, CoaXPress …) must be supported by the controller.

records.name: Controller and servo drive share a fieldbus

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF the drive needs EtherCAT / PROFINET / EtherNet-IP THEN the selected controller must support it.

records.name: Servo drive rating covers the motor

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: IF motor rated power > drive rated power THEN incompatible. Confirm the manufacturer’s drive/motor pairing table as well.

records.name: Scanner and controller share a command protocol

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: Scanner command protocol (XY2-100, SL2-100 …) must be supported by the controller.

records.name: Laser and controller share a control interface

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: The laser control interface (DB25, RS232, Ethernet …) must be supported by the controller.

records.name: Gripper weight within robot payload

provenance.note: Engineering rule written from the master prompt §44 examples. A rule result is an engineering inference, never a manufacturer confirmation. Review before relying on it.

records.explanation: Tool weight (plus part weight) must stay within the robot payload at the tool’s centre of gravity.
